intended_object: The canonical identification of a coupling π of two probability measures μ₀, μ₁ on X 0 × X 1 with a multi-marginal coupling indexed by Fin 2. The coupling π is pushed forward to the dependent product ∀ i : Fin 2, X i along the inverse of the canonical isomorphism with the binary product. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the underlying measure of π and maps it along `(MeasurableEquiv.piFinTwo X).symm`. That map is the measurable bijection X 0 × X 1 ≃ ∀ i : Fin 2, X i, sending (a, b) to the function i ↦ (a if i = 0, b if i = 1).

The lemma `isMultiCoupling_piFinTwo` checks that the i-th coordinate marginal of the result is μ i. The file also proves that the round trip through `toCouplingFinTwo` gives back π. So the definition is exactly the natural map from two-marginal couplings to Fin 2-indexed multi-marginal couplings.

Fixing the index type to `Fin 2` is not too narrow: the construction is precisely the comparison between the binary-product API and the Fin 2 case of the dependent-product API, so it needs this setting. The general multi-marginal notion is defined separately for arbitrary ι. Mathlib has no coupling API, so there is no counterpart.
